newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - December 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - December 20.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
The Hindustan Times
RAO RESIGNS AS CONGRESS PARLIAMENTARY PARTY CHIEF

Former premier P.V. Narasimha Rao finally bowed out as the Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP) leader while senior leaders began to work for a consensus successor to avoid rivalry in the party. Their efforts were guided by the growing realisation that Rao's exit meant that the United Front government's days would be limited and the choice of the new CPP leader would determine the role of the Congress in future. Their effort appeared to be directed at making Congress president Sitaram Kesri as the uncontested CPP leader. Indian Express
COURT OVERTURNS PRESIDENT'S RULE IN UTTAR PRADESH

The Allahabad High Court quashed the Presidential proclamation imposing President's rule in Uttar Pradesh, saying it was unconstitutional. The order, however, would come into force from December 26 to enable the government to challenge the ruling in the Supreme Court. In Parliament, the Bharatiya Janata Party hailed the court verdict and demanded that the United Front government should resign as it had no moral right to continue. Union Law Minister Ramakant Khalap, however, said the government would appeal against the verdict in the Supreme Court. The Uttar Pradesh government also said it would file a Special Leave Petition in the apex court challenging the verdict.
The Economic Times
BANKS TO REINVIGORATE STOCK MARKETS

To prop up the sagging stock market, banks have decided to invest in various schemes of the Unit Trust of India (UTI). Some of them, like Bank of Baroda, are seeking exemption from an investment limit of five percent of incremental deposits imposed by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). UTI sources expect the banks would immediately invest in open-ended equity funds like the Grandmaster 93 and the Primary Equity Fund.
DELHI GOVERNMENT APPROVES 300-MW APOLLO UNIT

Apollo Energy received the go-ahead from the Delhi government for its proposed 300 MW power project to be located in Delhi. The project would be one of the first in the private sector to use the circulating fluidised bed technology, which would enable it to produce power with very low levels of ash and emission. When completed around the year 2000, it would be the cleanest and most environment-friendly thermal power project in the country, company sources said.
RBI SLASHES REPO RATES

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) reduced the rate of interest at which liquidity support, in the form of repo transactions, would be provided to primary dealers. An RBI release said liquidity support against the 91-day treasury bills would be provided at 10.50 percent per annum, against 11.50 percent earlier and at 11 percent for Government of India dated securities against 13 percent previously. The revised rates of interest would be effective from Thursday, it said.
Financial Express
KERB DEALS END HIGHER

Pivotals jumped up in kerb deals on the Bombay Stock Exchange following the news of resignation of ex-premier Narasimha Rao from the post of Congress Parliamentary Party leader. In hectic kerb trading, Reliance Industries jumped to 199-200 rupees from the day's close of 197.50 rupees. State Bank of India was quoted at 223-24 rupees from the day's close of 221.50 rupees, ITC Ltd at 286.50-87 rupees from close of 285 rupees and Tata Iron and Steel was quoted higher at 163.50-164 rupees from close of 161 rupees.
SUZUKI WANTS 74 PCT STAKE IN MARUTI

Suzuki Motor corporation (SMC) offered to invest a fresh sum of 80 billion rupees in new automobile projects in joint ventures with the government. However, the Japanese automobile major demanded a 74 percent stake in Maruti Udyog Ltd (MUL) in return. SMC president O Suzuki, in his meeting with Industry Minister Murasoli Maran, offered to make investments in greenfield sites in West Bengal and Tamil Nadu. Sources said Suzuki's offer for setting up a manufacturing site in West Bengal was aimed at striking a rapport with the Left parties which could possibly oppose disinvestment of government's stake in MUL.
INSURANCE WATCHDOG BILL SEEKS STATUTORY POWERS

The Insurance Regulatory Authority (IRA) Bill seeks to set up a seven-member IRA as a statutory body. IRA would be set up on the lines of the Securities and Exchange Board of India, with powers to control investments, undertake audits and prescribe formats of book-keeping for insurance companies. The IRA Bill is likely to be introduced in the Parliament by the Finance Minister P. Chidambaram on Friday. The proposed Bill, however, would fall short of the expectations of the private sector as there is no explicit proposal to permit IRA to grant licences to new entrants.
CLEAR EXIT POLICY FOR BANKING SECTOR SOUGHT

The Reserve Bank of India's deputy governor Y.V. Reddy called for a clear exit policy in the banking industry. At a bank economists' conference, he pointed out that the entry norms were fairly clear in the banking industry but exit norms were not. Accepting the industry's demand for more freedom, Reddy called for strategic alliances among commercial banks. He, however, warned the banks against cartelisation.
TELCO, MERCEDES RELATIONSHIP ON THE ROCKS

The tie-up between Tata Electric Locomotive Company (Telco) and Mercedes-Benz India Ltd is heading for a break-up. A clue to the impending rift is available from Mercedes-Benz's decision to set up its own marketing set-up independent of Telco. Currently, the E 220 petrol and E 250 diesel Mercedes Benz cars made by the joint venture are marketed through the Telco network. The creation of a dedicated marketing and sales function implies that Metcedes Benz is keen on kicking off its own dealer network.
Business Standard
BUYBACK PLAN FOR PROMOTERS VIA TRUST SPIKED

The law ministry rejected the Securities and Exchange Board of India's (SEBI) proposal to allow buyback of shares through the trust route to shore up the capital market. The SEBI proposal had been referred to the law ministry since the trusts had been allowed market-making in odd lot shares and in that sense, the proposal was considered to be only an extension of the same principle. The law ministry said the trust route could be opened up only by amending the Companies Act and it should not be done independently, but as part of the recodification process.
BAT DEMAND FOR ITC PROBE PANEL QUESTIONED

Some of the financial institution (FI) nominees on the ITC board have questioned the need for a separate inquiry committee to investigate the alleged Foreign Exchange Regulation Act (FERA) violations by the top executives. FI sources said the matter was being already investigated by the Enforcement Directorate. Earlier, BAT Plc had demanded setting up of a separate inquiry committee to probe into FERA violations by tobacco major's top executives.
Business Line
JOINT SECTOR POWER PROJECTS HOLD KEY

The power ministry has decided to encourage federal and state government power companies to go in for joint ventures with multinationals. The move is aimed at tackling the problem of an acute shortage of funds which would make it difficult to achieve the Ninth Plan target of 25,000 MW generating capacity in the public sector. The target was mooted in the approach paper for the Ninth Plan. Power minister S Venugopalachari, however, said the majority stake holding would be with the Indian company.
The Observer
PETROLEUM PRODUCTS MAY COST MORE IN JANUARY

The finance ministry is understood to have decided to announce a revision in the prices of diesel, liquified petroleum gas and petrol in January 1997. Sources said the announcement could come some time early next year for which a special cabinet meeting was expected to be convened in the last week of December. This was because the government could no longer afford the mounting oil pool account, which was expected to touch 160 billion rupees, as also the oil import bill, which might exceed 300 billion rupees by the end of the fiscal 1996/97 (April-March), if the existing petro-products' prices were not revised.
